key_concepts: Reproduction is the ability of a living thing to continue the existence of its kind.
Sexual reproduction involves sex cells from two parents uniting to form a new individual.
Asexual reproduction involves only one parent producing identical copies of itself.
Male gonads are testes and produce sperm; female gonads are ovaries and produce eggs.
Sperm and egg cells are called gametes.
Fertilization is the union of a sperm cell and an egg cell.
The fertilized egg is a zygote that develops into an embryo.
Internal fertilization occurs inside the female's body, as in dogs and cats.
External fertilization occurs outside the body, usually in water, as in frogs and mosquito
Butterfly reproduction begins with courtship and male pheromones.
Frogs use a mating posture called amplexus so sperm reach eggs released in water.
Dogs and cats have a heat cycle called estrus.
